newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson shares seen falling after results.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson shares seen falling after results.

text.p: Shares in Swedish telecoms group AB LM Ericsson could fall back after the company releases its 1996 earnings on Tuesday, analyst said on Monday.

"We currently have a valuation situation for this type of shares that means companies have to beat expectations significantly to uphold the share price and push it higher," Johan Strandberg, analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, told Reuters.
He did not, however, forecast a large drop in the share price.
"If earnings are roughly in line with expectations, around 9.9-10.0 billion crowns, there is a risk of disappointment but I do not believe in a slide," he said.
Ulf Hellzen, analyst at Swedbank, said that expectations were high ahead of the report.
"The share has a high valuation and the market is expecting a strong report...I believe that forecasts are too high," he said.
A Reuters poll of 18 analysts found expectations of a pre-tax profit of 10.03 billion crowns for 1996 compared to 7.62 billion crowns in 1995.
Profit per share was forecast to rise to 6.95 crowns while sales revenue was forecast at 117.50 billion crowns.
But in general, analysts saw a share dip as temporary as investors would be attracted by the sector's strong growth, which is expected to continue for a long period of time.
"There is a higher likelihood that the share will fall rather than rise on the report, but I see that fall as temporary," an analyst said.
Apart from Ericsson's profit, its fourth quarter order intake will be scrutinised, analysts said.
"Order intake will be a positive detail," said Strandberg. "It has been very strong in the fourth quarter."
Other important details are how the group's margins have developed and how order intake at the company's public telecommunications unit has developed.
Hellzen said Ericsson's public telecoms unit, which has a relatively low profitability, normally has large fourth quarter sales which will show in the group's operating margin.
Ericsson is due to present earnings around 1100 GMT on Tuesday. Its share rose eight crowns to 252 during Monday trade.
